reader.requirement: At --std 85 every successfully executed input-output statement on an indexed file (OPEN, CLOSE, READ random/sequential/dynamic, WRITE, REWRITE, START, DELETE) must leave a successful-completion I-O status (first digit 0: 00, or 02/04/05 where their conditions hold) and, being successful, must not execute any USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION procedure.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.IndexedDuplicateKeyStatusSequentialOnly (changed 2002): at 85 a random READ by an alternate key whose next record has the same key answers 02, from 2002 only a sequential READ does
DialectBehavior.FileSharingFacility (2002): at 85 no connector restricts another, so OPENs of a second connector succeed with 00
bakes the --std edition into the file connector (FileConnector.Edition) that the two behaviours above read

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: a random READ by an alternate key with a following duplicate gives 02 at 85 (as §1985:IX.1.3.4's 02 item, 'For a READ statement', names no access mode) and 00 at 2023; every other success status takes the same arm

reader.notes: Successful statements report 00/02/05 and never reach the USE machinery. LEAD (not this row; for 1985-GR-IX.1.3.4-L2.1 and 1985-GR-IX.4.5.4-18): kb/Work PB5480 (landed) added the 04 arm but it fires only for a RECORD VARYING reader; a fixed-size indexed reader that reads a longer record written by another connector on a file it opened while zero-byte gets 00 (io4d: RR-IB 00 001abcdefg) where the varying twin gets 04 (io4e). Site: IndexedConnector.IndexedReadStatus / FileConnector.RecordLengthConflicts fixed arm; PB5480 records that two concurrent connectors are a 1985-undefined setup.

refuter.evidence: Probe refute-1985-088/src/p5.cob at --std 85 (run p5-001) covers what io1 did not. A prime-key sequential READ NEXT over records that share an alternate key gave 00 for each (PN1/PN2), not 02. A random READ by the prime key gave 00. A random READ KEY IS AK gave 02, and the READ NEXTs that followed gave 02 and then 00 at the last duplicate. START KEY GREATER gave 00. Sequential-access READ, REWRITE and DELETE on a second connector gave 00. OPEN EXTEND of an absent OPTIONAL indexed file gave 05, its WRITE gave 00, and the file was created (re-read 00 100). USE-COUNT stayed 0. One reading point that does not decide this row: a REWRITE that leaves an already duplicated alternate key value unchanged gave 00, not 02; both are successful-completion values, and the 02 item is a sub-item of its own. cite.py: OK §1985:IX.1.3.4 GR1 the text is in GR1.
